sections.content:
Before midterm:
Basic market intro, LOB, order types

After midterm:
Roll's model, G-M's model, Kyle's model etc.

It is a very good introduction course to the secondary market especially in trading and market microstructure. You learn the mathematical models but get the intuition for real trading. I saw someone wrote that it contains a lot of math. Yes, but definitely not beyond MATH2421. If you did Gaokao, the algebra of this course is just high school level.
sections.teaching: The professor's research area is market microstructure, so he is very knowledgeable in this area. He illustrates the contents clearly. Do not skip classes because he will cover many points not on the slides.
sections.grading:
Assignments: 20%
Midterm Exam: 25%
Final Exam: 55%

Midterm is easy and similar to assignments and practice questions. Final is hard with tight time, but still managable if you are good at math.
sections.workload: Light. Only 3 assignments and reviewing for midterm and final.

sections.content:
Introduction
Overview of General Market Structures
Orders and Quotes
Players in Financial Markets
US Market Structure and Trading Rules
Platform Architectures
Microstructure Data Issues

After midterm exam
Information in Finance (w/ math prep)
Models of Price Dynamics
Measuring Liquidity
Order Size and Strategic Trading
High-Frequency Trading

The first part of the course covers the financial market microstructure, including LOB, different types of orders and trading rules, which I think if you actually trade on your own, you will know some of these and a lot of this will feel like common sense dressed up in jargon.

The second part focuses on different theoretical models: Roll's, Glosten-Milgrom (single/multi period), Stoll, Kyle and maybe more. These models have different initial settings and a bunch of different unrealistic assumptions that I don't think people would actually use them in workplace or real life application. The professor also mentioned in class this is a bridging course to phd degree. The second part is extremely heavy in maths (there is a math prep after midterm content) so if you are not confident with your maths or algebra, do not even think about taking it (most of the maths are algebra as well, its hell).

So yeah, you’ll grind through the math, learn some intuition about information asymmetry or what forms the bid-ask spread, and then promptly forget 90 % of the specific formulas the moment you start trading or working on a real desk.

sections.content:
I think the content of the course has been adjusted over the years - NO CODING.

This course covers topics that would be useful for traders to understand the structure of a market (but mostly theoratical discussion with many assumptions):

1. Trading Mechanism and Market Structure
2. Information Theory
3. Model of Price Dynamics
    - The Roll Model of Prices
4. Information in Financial Market
    - Glosten-Milgrom Model
    - Stoll Model of inventory cost
5. Measuring and Estimating Liquidity
    - Kyle Model
6. Regulation and Policy Issues
7. High-Frequency Trading

I think the most diffcult part about this course is that the content is niche. It's very hard for me to find learning resources online even if i want to self-study (e.g. you can easily find CAPM online, but not the glosten-milgrom model). So this course relies heavily on your understanding during the class. I don't find this course easy to be honest.

In addition, sometimes i find it hard to listen to him due to his pronounciation/ accent (especially when i sit at the back of the classroom)

sections.content: The content is extremely easy. The course covers almost everything you need to know to become a trader! However, the content itself is not deep enough. So if you are planning to become a trader, further self-study is a must!
sections.teaching:
Teaching is acceptable. However, the lecture notes are just disaster.
There are many typos within the lecture slides and the professor only corrects those mistakes during lecture time. P.S There are even wrong solutions for both the mock midterm exam and final exam! My advice to the warriors that are planning to take this course is "Don't believe what you see and hear whether it is on the lecture slides or directly coming out from professor's mouth". Professor himself is a typo.
sections.grading:
The grading is the only satisfactory part of this course!
22% A
60% B
18% C
In the end, he gave me A-! So Professor typo is still recommended if you are looking for gpa boost.
